subject: MA Plan cadence: priority support request & temporary SLA exception
messages:
From: Jamie Park <jamie@piedmontanalytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@piedmontanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-10 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff: production cutover timeline & SLA exception request

Mina / Redwood team —

Thanks for the quick sync last week. We ran the last integration pass overnight and are seeing intermittent 95th/99th percentile latency spikes when payloads hit ~6k tokens. That has put our production cutover at risk for next Tuesday (4/13).

To avoid missing our committed go-live date, Piedmont is requesting:
- Temporary SLA exception (target: relax 99.9% latency SLA to 99.5% for 7 days) to allow a staged canary while we fix the tokenization edge case.
- Priority support (response within 1 hour for severity >= P2) during the cutover window.

Attached are the integration logs and a short timeline we propose. We want to lock a weekly MAP checkpoint cadence (Tuesdays 10am PT) to track progress and ensure executive sponsors are updated if any SLA exceptions are needed.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Redwood to confirm whether SLA exception is approved and list conditions.
2) Technical dive between our SRE and Redwood infra team (we can do 4/10 2pm PT).
3) Sign-off on MA Plan v3 so we can proceed with canary.

Can you confirm direction and next steps?

Thanks,
Jamie Park
Head of Integrations — Piedmont Analytics
Attachments: integration-logs-20270409.zip
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@piedmontanalytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Alex Torres <alex.torres@piedmontanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-10 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: production cutover timeline & SLA exception request

Jamie —

Thanks for the details and the logs. Appreciate the heads-up. Short answer: we can support a temporary SLA carve-out and priority incident routing for the cutover, but we need to lock a few items on the MA Plan and attach conditional acceptance to the exception.

Immediate confirmations and next steps (action owners shown):
- Redwood will provision priority incident routing and assign a dedicated on-call for the cutover window (owner: mina_haddad).
- Karthik will lead the technical dive today and produce a remediation runbook by EOD (owner: karthik_iyer).
- We will draft an SLA exception letter with conditions (owner: marissa_cole) and circulate for signature.
- Piedmont to finalize the MAP v3 doc and confirm cutover date (owner: jamie@piedmontanalytics.com).

I attached an editable MAP_v3_20270410.docx with suggested placeholders for the SLA carve-out and rollback criteria. We agree to the Tuesday weekly checkpoint at 10am PT — I’ve tentatively booked a recurring invite pending your confirmation.

Can Karthik and I join the 2pm PT dive? If so, please send a calendar invite and include the relevant trace IDs and a minimal repro.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | mina.haddad@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0133

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: FW: MAP kickoff: production cutover timeline & SLA exception request

Team —

Forwarding Piedmont's request and Mina's confirmation. High-level triage notes from the morning debug:
- Root cause hypothesis: tokenizer shard path that mishandles certain emoji+whitespace sequences leading to excessive KV cache misses at longer contexts (~6k tokens).
- Repro is consistent using trace IDs provided; reproduces on both our internal canary infra and customer's environment.
- Quick mitigation we can push: forced prefix-normalization + temporary cache warming on canary nodes. This reduces 95th/99th spikes but not completely.

Asking for two escalations now:
1) Approval to provision a dedicated canary pool with autoscale bump for the 72-hour window (cost covered by Piedmont under deal terms) — owner: marissa_cole to sign off on capacity change.
2) Exec-level approval for the temporary SLA exception language before we send it to the customer — owner: soojin_lee to approve the wording and conditions.

I’ll prepare a short technical runbook (steps + rollbacks) and paste into the MAP doc. Mina — can you confirm when we have the capacity bump online?

-Karthik

Jamie / Alex —

Following internal review, Redwood will grant a time-limited SLA exception as requested. Summary of approval and conditions:

- Exception window: 2027-04-12 00:00 PT through 2027-04-18 23:59 PT (7 days).
- Adjusted target: 99.5% latency availability for the exception window; all other SLA terms remain unchanged.
- Conditions (must be met before exception is active):
  1) Signed MA Plan v3 with rollback criteria and cutover checklist in place.
  2) Provisioning of dedicated canary pool and confirmation of autoscale bump.
  3) Piedmont to provide final repro traces and agree to the incident triage cadence.
- Redwood obligations during the window: dedicated on-call escalation (owner: mina_haddad), 1-hour response for Severity >= P2, daily health report to Piedmont and map checkpoints.

We will circulate a short SLA-exception-letter for signature (attached). This exception is revocable if any of the conditions are not met.

Soojin Lee
